outcome: Nothing published since 26 January 2024 settles or moves the bounded-density or bounded-separation question for Danzer sets. The in-window work on the nearby object (Kashkan, arXiv 2407.01633, June 2024; reported in Mathematika 2025) constructs dense forests, a weaker object, and the in-window items carrying the Danzer name concern different problems (Erdos 224 and Erdos 1071).
problem_asks: Statement: 'Danzer's problem and Conway's dead fly problem - do Danzer sets of bounded density or bounded separation exist?' Unpacked: (a) Does a Danzer set of bounded density exist? A Danzer set is a set Y in R^d meeting every convex body of volume 1. The sources read 'bounded density' as finite upper density, limsup over R of #(Y intersect B(0,R)) / R^d < infinity, equivalently growth O(T^d) (Wikipedia: growth O(r^d); Solomon-Weiss: growth T^d). (b) Does a Danzer set of bounded separation exist? Conway's formulation as the sources give it: a Danzer set whose points are separated by a bounded distance from each other (read as uniform discreteness: a positive lower bound on pairwise distances). The sources add that such a set would also be a Delone set (bounded gaps too), and that a positive answer would also answer (a). The statement does not name the dimension d; the literature treats every d >= 2. Note that the statement asks two things, so a result settling only (a), or only (b), settles only part of the bullet.

events.what_happened: Yaar Solomon and Barak Weiss, 'Dense forests and Danzer sets', arXiv 1406.3807. Shows that Delone sets from primitive polygonal substitution tilings (including the vertex set of a Penrose tiling) and finite unions of cut-and-project sets are not Danzer sets (Thm 1.1, 1.2). Constructs uniformly discrete dense forests in R^d for every d via homogeneous dynamics and Ratner's theorems (Thm 1.3). States an equivalence (Thm 1.4): for d >= 2 and polynomial growth g, a Danzer set of growth g exists iff eps-nets of size O(g(eps^(-1/d))) exist for boxes in [0,1]^d. Derives Danzer sets of growth T^d log T (Thm 1.6), improving O(T^d log^(d-1) T). Published Annales scientifiques de l'ENS 49(5), 2016, pp. 1053-1074 (journal page not opened; from search metadata).
events.revisions: arXiv ID 1406 gives June 2014 for v1 (v1 date not opened); v2 submitted 10 Jul 2014 per the fetched arXiv page; journal version Annales ENS 2016.
events.delivers: Restricted to classes of sets. Shows several natural candidate classes contain no Danzer set. Constructs a weaker object (uniformly discrete dense forests, finite density in the relaxed sense). Best known growth for a Danzer set in this paper is O(T^d log T), which is finite growth but not the O(T^d) that bounded density requires. Does not give a Danzer set of bounded density.
events.remains: (a) bounded density: open, since the paper says it is not known whether Danzer sets in R^d with growth O(T^d) exist. (b) bounded separation: the paper's section 4 says 'we do not know whether the dense forest constructed in section 4 is a Danzer set'; no separation result.

events.direction: Negative for several natural classes of candidate sets; positive for a weaker relaxed-density object and for finite (non-bounded) growth. Neither proves nor disproves the bounded-density existence question.
events.object: Not a single object. (i) Negative results for Delone substitution-tiling vertex sets (including Penrose) and finite unions of cut-and-project sets. (ii) Uniformly discrete dense forests in R^d built as return-time sets of a completely uniquely ergodic flow (cross-section of the flow). (iii) Danzer sets of growth T^d log T, obtained through the epsilon-net equivalence of Thm 1.4; per Kashkan's 2024 conclusion (as reported by a summarising fetch) this construction is random, not explicit.

events.what_happened: David Simmons and Yaar Solomon, 'A Danzer set for axis parallel boxes', arXiv 1409.0926. Explicit discrete point sets in R^d (d >= 2) that meet every axis-parallel box of volume 1, with growth O(T^d), described by the authors as optimal. The arXiv abstract page lists no journal reference; search metadata reports a later publication in Proc. AMS 2016, not checked.
events.revisions: v1 3 Sep 2014; v2 21 Jan 2015; v3 18 Aug 2015 (version shown on the fetched page).
events.delivers: Restricted class: sets that meet every axis-parallel box of volume 1 (not every convex body), with optimal O(T^d) growth. The arXiv abstract page makes no claim about convex bodies, about John's theorem, or about equivalence with the convex-body Danzer problem. A transfer from aligned boxes to all convex bodies is not established by the page I read. (One search summary asserted such an equivalence via John's theorem; the page does not support that, so I have not relied on it.)
events.remains: (a) for convex bodies, bounded density: open per Wikipedia and the Solomon-Weiss abstract. (b) bounded separation: not addressed.
events.time_since_posted: about 12 years; no review or follow-up found in searches (not checked against citing papers in full)
events.doubts: Scope, not correctness: the sets meet aligned boxes only. Wikipedia still lists the convex-body question as open, which is consistent with the aligned-box class not transferring. I have not read the full text, so I cannot say whether the paper itself discusses the transfer.
events.direction: Positive for the aligned-box class at the optimal exponent T^d. For the convex-body question as stated in the bullet it is silent.
events.object: Explicit construction of discrete point sets in R^d (d >= 2) meeting every axis-parallel box of volume 1, with growth O(T^d). Explicit, per the abstract as summarised. The full construction was not read.

events.what_happened: Omri Solan, Yaar Solomon and Barak Weiss, 'On problems of Danzer and Gowers and dynamics on the space of closed subsets of R^d', arXiv 1510.07179. Proves that no set Y in R^d exists such that every convex set of volume one meets Y in a number of points bounded above and below by nonzero constants (answering Gowers' question of 2000). Gives a second, short proof, and a quantitative consequence: every eps-net for convex sets in [0,1]^d has a convex set of volume eps containing at least Omega(log log(1/eps)) of its points. Published International Mathematics Research Notices 2017 (vol 2017, no 21, pp 6584-6598; from search metadata and the Wikipedia article).
events.revisions: v1 only, submitted 24 Oct 2015 (per fetched arXiv page); IMRN 2017.
events.delivers: Gowers' strengthening only: Danzer sets whose intersection counts with unit-volume convex bodies are uniformly bounded (two-sided) do not exist. This is a stronger counting requirement, not a density or separation condition. Establishes nothing about whether a Danzer set of bounded density or bounded separation exists.
events.remains: (a) bounded density: open. (b) bounded separation: open. The paper gives no positive density or separation result.

checked_by.what_they_did: Published the paper in 2017 (publication from the Wikipedia article and search metadata; the IMRN page itself was not opened)
checked_by.where: https://arxiv.org/abs/1510.07179 (arXiv opened); IMRN page not opened

events.time_since_posted: about 11 years; published 2017; no challenge to the result found
events.direction: Negative, for Gowers' bounded-count variant. Silent on the density and separation questions.

events.what_happened: Faustin Adiceam, 'Around the Danzer problem and the construction of dense forests', arXiv 2010.06756. A survey of known results on Danzer's problem and on dense forests, which it says it generalises in places and for which it lists open problems. Published L'Enseignement Mathematique 68 (2022), no 1/2, pp 25-60, DOI 10.4171/LEM/1020. The abstract calls the problem 'a longstanding question' and aims to 'make further progress towards a solution'. This is a survey, not a result.
events.revisions: v1 14 Oct 2020; v2 20 Oct 2020; v3 5 Nov 2020; v4 30 Mar 2021 (current, per fetched arXiv page). Journal version 2022 (EMS page gives 'submitted 6 November 2020, published 29 March 2022').
events.delivers: Survey: no new result on bounded density or separation claimed in the abstract page read. Full text not read.
events.remains: (a) and (b) both, as the survey itself lists them as open.
events.direction: Neutral: states the problem as open and lists open problems.

events.what_happened: Ioannis Tsokanos, 'Danzer's problem, effective constructions of dense forests and digital sequences', arXiv 2111.02773 (one version, 12 pages). Gives a deterministic dense forest with the best known visibility bound (deterministic and effective, unlike earlier constructions); introduces optical forests (optimal visibility, density not necessarily finite, finite only up to a logarithm); gives a planar Peres-type dense forest with the best known visibility bound. Search metadata lists Mathematika 2022 (Wiley DOI 10.1112/mtk.12153); the journal page was not opened.
events.revisions: One version (v1), submitted 4 Nov 2021, per fetched arXiv page.
events.delivers: Concerns dense forests and optical forests only, in dimensions d >= 2 and in the plane. Does not claim a Danzer set of bounded density or bounded separation.
events.direction: Neutral to the problem; positive for the relaxed objects only.
events.object: A deterministic discrete set of finite density in R^d (d >= 2) with the best known visibility function, plus an optical forest and a planar Peres-type forest. Explicit (deterministic digital-sequence construction). The abstract gives no formula, and the full text was not read.

events.what_happened: Kirill Kashkan, 'A New Construction of Forests with Low Visibility', arXiv 2407.01633. Builds a set of finite density in R^d (d >= 2) by adding points to a Poisson point process, such that every line segment of length on the order of eps^(-(d-1)) ln(1/eps) comes within distance eps of a point; the constant depends only on d. The conclusion states that 'in dimension greater than 2, a dense forest is not necessarily a Danzer set' (the HTML rendering shows '22', which I read as a formatting artefact for 2). The conclusion attributes to reference [9] the conjecture that the Rote-Tichy lower bound for the equivalent epsilon-net problem is best possible, 'implying a negative answer to Danzer's problem'. Reported as published in Mathematika 71(2), Paper No. e70013, 2025 (from a search summary of the author's thesis; Wiley page returned HTTP 403; not confirmed).
events.revisions: v1 29 Jun 2024; v2 22 Nov 2024; v3 16 Dec 2024 (current, per fetched arXiv page). Mathematika 2025 (reported, not verified).
events.delivers: A dense forest (a weaker, visibility-based object) of finite density in every d >= 2, with a logarithmic-factor visibility bound. Not a Danzer set: the paper itself notes that in dimension above 2 a dense forest need not be a Danzer set. A search summary reports a planar equivalence (a finite-density Danzer set in the plane exists iff a finite-density dense forest with visibility V(eps) << 1/eps exists); this paper's bound carries a log factor, so on my reading it does not reach that threshold in the plane. That reading is mine and unverified against the source for the equivalence.
events.remains: (a) bounded density: this paper does not address Danzer sets of any density. (b) bounded separation: not addressed. Also the conjecture cited from [9] remains a conjecture in this paper.

checked_by.what_they_did: Reported publication 2025 (from a search summary of the author's thesis; the Wiley page returned HTTP 403 and was not opened)
checked_by.where: Not established. Article number e70013 reported; no URL opened.

events.time_since_posted: about 16 months as of October 2026 (arXiv); journal publication reported 2025
events.doubts: No doubt about correctness found. The construction's visibility bound carries a logarithmic factor relative to the planar threshold in one search summary, which bears on scope rather than on correctness.
events.direction: Positive for the relaxed dense-forest question. Does not cut toward or against the existence of a Danzer set of bounded density or bounded separation.
events.object: A dense forest in R^d (d >= 2): a set of finite density built by adding points to a Poisson base process, so that every long enough segment approaches the set within eps. The construction is probabilistic (Poisson base), not explicit, per the abstract as summarised. The conclusion's conjecture is stated, not proved, in this paper.

events.what_happened: Kirill Kashkan, PhD thesis 'Dense Forests with Low Visibility', University of Toronto. The thesis PDF is on the Toronto mathematics site, but both copies I tried returned a human-verification page and I could not read it. A search summary reports: the dense-forest result of arXiv 2407.01633; a relaxed Danzer question in which the volume bound may grow with the eccentricity of the convex set; a Poisson base set that can be adjusted to be uniformly discrete; and a defence scheduled for 9 September 2025.
events.delivers: Not established. The reported relaxed-Danzer variant (volume allowed to grow with eccentricity) may be new relative to the arXiv paper, but I could not read its statement or proof, so I cannot say what it establishes.
events.remains: Unknown. Bounded density and bounded separation are presumably untouched, but this is not verified.

checked_by.who: University of Toronto doctoral committee (defence reported in a search summary; not verified)

events.doubts: I could not read the thesis, so I cannot assess the reported relaxed-Danzer result. It is the main unread lead in this record.
events.direction: Unknown for the bounded-density and bounded-separation questions.

events.what_happened: Eduard Stefanescu, 'On the maximal volume of empty convex bodies amidst multivariate dilates of a lacunary integer sequence', arXiv 2504.03575 (versions 4 Apr 2025 to 25 Aug 2025). For a Hadamard-lacunary integer sequence and almost every dilation vector alpha in [0,1]^d, every convex set in [0,1]^d of volume at least (log N)^(2+eps)/N contains a point of {alpha a_n mod 1 : n <= N}, for large N; claimed optimal up to logarithmic factors. The content read contains no mention of Danzer sets, dense forests, or the density or separation question.
events.revisions: v1 4 Apr 2025; v2 8 Apr 2025; v3 13 May 2025; v4 9 Jun 2025; v5 25 Aug 2025 (per fetched arXiv page).
events.delivers: A hitting statement for finite N-point sets in the cube at threshold volume (log N)^(2+eps)/N, for almost every alpha. It concerns finite point sets and convex sets in [0,1]^d. It does not concern infinite Danzer sets in R^d, and says nothing about their density or separation.
events.direction: Neither way for the problem. A finite hitting result at a volume threshold.

events.what_happened: Ilay Hoshen and Wojciech Samotij, 'Optimal lower bounds for epsilon-nets for lines in the plane', arXiv 2608.11457, submitted 11 Aug 2026 (single version). For arbitrarily small eps there is a finite planar point set whose line-induced range space needs eps-nets of size Omega((1/eps) log(1/eps)), matching the Haussler-Welzl upper bound and confirming a prediction of Alon. Concerns lines, not convex bodies or boxes; does not mention Danzer.
events.revisions: Single version, 11 Aug 2026 (per fetched arXiv page).
events.delivers: A lower bound for epsilon-nets of line-induced range spaces in the plane. Not boxes and not convex sets, so not the epsilon-net side of the Danzer equivalence (which Solomon-Weiss state for boxes in [0,1]^d).

events.what_happened: A different problem sharing a namesake: Erdos Problem 224 (the Danzer-Grunbaum obtuse-angle problem): any set of 2^d+1 points in R^d determines an obtuse angle. The general case is due to Danzer and Grunbaum (1962). In January 2026 a Lean 4 (mathlib) formalisation was posted to the Erdos forum (thread 224; poster 'Coder-Osman', 14-15 Jan 2026; files in the SpringSense Innovation Institute repository). The poster, as reported by a summarising fetch of the thread, says the formalisation was 'mainly done by AI and AI-powered agents': the natural-language proof sketch and coarse Lean framework were generated by GPT-5.2 Thinking, and a Codex agent iteratively eliminated the sorrys. The erdosproblems AI-contributions wiki lists this entry as 'Codex, GPT-5.2 Thinking' dated 14 Jan 2026, with the literature entry 'Danzer and Grunbaum (1962)'.
events.revisions: Forum posts 28 Oct 2025 to 15 Jan 2026 (per summary); Lean files uploaded 15 Jan 2026.
events.delivers: A formalisation of a 1962 theorem on obtuse angles in point sets. A different question: it says nothing about convex bodies of volume one, density, or separation of Danzer sets.

events.what_happened: A different problem sharing a namesake: Erdos Problem 1071 concerns maximal families of disjoint unit line segments in a region. Danzer is credited with the first example (Erdos paid Danzer $10); the second part (a countably infinite maximal set in the unit square) is credited to a comment by Boris Alexeev. The AI-contributions wiki lists a formalisation credited to 'Danzer; Alexeev (2026)' in the formalisation column with systems 'Aleph Prover, Aristotle, GPT', dated 29 Jan 2026 (second part) and 12 Feb 2026 (first part). The erdosproblems page is marked PROVED (LEAN).

events.delivers: Not about Danzer sets. The result concerns unit segments in regions and says nothing about convex bodies of volume one or point sets.
events.direction: Affirmative for its own question. Not relevant to the Danzer-set direction.

summary: Across 44 web searches and 21 page fetches, I found no event since 26 January 2024 that settles, or moves, the bounded-density or bounded-separation question for Danzer sets. The problem is still treated as open by the current Wikipedia article (fetched via a summarising tool, which reports a last-edit date of 22 June 2026 that I could not confirm), by Adiceam's 2022 survey, and by the 2024 Kashkan paper. The earlier-dated core is: Solomon and Weiss (2014) for the best known growth O(T^d log T) and the equivalence to epsilon-nets for boxes; Simmons and Solomon (2014) for optimal-growth sets for aligned boxes only; Solan, Solomon and Weiss (2015, IMRN 2017) for the negative answer to Gowers' bounded-count variant, which is a different and stronger counting condition. The only in-window work on the Danzer object is Kashkan's arXiv 2407.01633 (June 2024, revised to December 2024, reported in Mathematika 2025), which constructs dense forests of finite density and explicitly notes that in dimension above 2 a dense forest need not be a Danzer set; it does not address Danzer sets of any density. A thesis by the same author (Toronto, reported defence 9 September 2025) reportedly contains a relaxed Danzer question with volume allowed to grow with eccentricity; I could not read it, so I record it as the main unread lead. The in-window items under the Danzer name that are AI-linked (Erdos 224, the Danzer-Grunbaum obtuse-angle formalisation credited to GPT-5.2 Thinking and Codex in January 2026; Erdos 1071) are on different problems and are recorded as namesake events only. Two in-window neighbours (Stefanescu 2025 on empty convex bodies amid lacunary dilates; Hoshen and Samotij 2026 on epsilon-nets for lines) do not mention Danzer sets and are recorded as discarded neighbours. Close calls: (1) Simmons-Solomon 2014 reaches the optimal exponent, which a reader could treat as progress on the density question; I read it as restricted to aligned boxes, since a convex body of volume one need not contain a large aligned box, and the arXiv page makes no transfer claim. Wikipedia's continued treatment of the question as open supports that reading, but I have not read the full text. One earlier search summary asserted a John-theorem equivalence; the page I opened does not support it. (2) Kashkan 2024: a reader could treat the finite-density planar forest as narrowing the planar question. On my reading its visibility bound carries an extra logarithm, so it does not reach the planar threshold a search summary reports; that threshold is not checked against its source. AI search: I ran explicit searches for AI involvement (Danzer with GPT, Claude, Gemini, AlphaEvolve, LLM, AI-assisted arXiv, formal-conjectures, the Erdos AI-contributions wiki, and a Lean/sorry check). No source names a system in connection with Danzer sets or the dead-fly question, so for the problem itself no AI system is named. The Erdos wiki's entries concern the namesakes only. Quotes attributed to the forum thread and to the Erdos wiki came through summarising fetches and are marked as such; I did not verify them verbatim. Dispersion background (Rote-Tichy 1996, Bukh-Chao 2020 on empty boxes, Trodler-Volec-Vybiral 2023 on minimal dispersion) predates the window; I saw those only as search snippets and did not open them, and I found no in-window box epsilon-net lower bound. Conway's dead-fly question: the sources give a $1000 prize and call it open; I found no in-window work on the bounded-separation part at all.
competing_reading: Simmons and Solomon (2014) already solve the density question in substance: sets meeting every aligned box of volume 1 with optimal O(T^d) growth, if a John-type reduction to convex bodies holds (the search-summary claim). That reading would date the event to 2014, outside the window, and would make the problem solved before 2024. The arXiv abstract page I read says nothing about convex bodies, and Wikipedia still lists the question as open, so I think the reduction does not hold as stated. Equally, a reader could count Kashkan's 2024 finite-density planar forest as progress toward the planar form of Danzer's question; I read its visibility bound as too weak for that.
what_would_settle_it: (1) The full text of arXiv 1409.0926: whether it contains or cites any transfer from aligned boxes to all convex bodies of volume one, and whether its O(T^d) growth is claimed for convex sets. (2) The meaning of 'boxes' in Solomon-Weiss Theorem 1.4 (aligned or all), and whether optimal-size epsilon-nets for those boxes are established anywhere. (3) The Toronto thesis (Kashkan, 'Dense Forests with Low Visibility'): the statement and proof of the relaxed Danzer result, and its date. (4) The Mathematika version of arXiv 2407.01633: publication, article number, and any change from v3. (5) The slides or any written version of Adiceam's Sydney seminar of 8 May 2025, which promised 'new constructions'; no written version was found. (6) The Wikipedia revision history for 'Danzer set', to confirm the current status and any recent edits. (7) A date-sorted arXiv search for 'Danzer' and 'dense forest' across 2024-2026, which these tools could not run; search results were the only access.
